title: Safer hand: the familiar register for the Ampline home page
question: You asked for the familiar end. Three grounded directions from the conventional side, plus the category standard played straight against Anker, Belkin and UGREEN. You pick.

options.label: The Charging Lock Screen
options.lineage: the phone's own charging screen: percentage, battery fill, minutes to 80%
options.thesis: The store speaks the screen the shopper sees when the charger works.
options.viewport: A light screen with one huge figure: pick your device and the fill animates to the max watts the catalog can deliver it, with 'up to 65W' in the charging line; products below are battery-glyph rows with their watt figure filled in.
options.risk: Familiar to the point of invisible, and it can tip into an iOS imitation; the fill has to carry catalog watts, never invented charge times.

options.label: The Charging-Guide Diagram
options.lineage: the per-port split slide the category ships in every gallery (45W / 30W / 7.5W)
options.thesis: Every product drawn with a leader line to each port and the watts it gives.
options.viewport: A white sheet: your device on the left, leader lines fanning to the products that fit, each line labelled with the port's max output; the split-output table sits under it as the proof.
options.risk: Closest to the canon; it is only distinct through diagram discipline, and leader lines get crowded on a phone.

options.label: The Retail Box
options.lineage: the charger's own packaging: big watt figure on the front, compatibility icons on the side, what's in the box on the back
options.thesis: Every product shown as the box you pick up in the shop, front, side and back.
options.viewport: A box front at hero scale with the watt figure and the device picker as its side-panel compatibility strip; picking a device rotates the shelf's boxes to show the side that names it.
options.risk: Reads as packaging mockups if the fold language is faked, and the side-panel icon strip is the category's icon-row habit.

canonCard.label: The category standard, against Anker, Belkin and UGREEN
canonCard.thesis: What the three best reference stores ship, at their craft level, with the device picker where Belkin's Choose Your Device menu would sit.
canonCard.viewport: A product-render hero with one line and a Shop Now pill, the device picker as a chip row under it, a category tile row, a best-sellers card shelf with strike-through prices, a trust row, a dark footer.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design; it also needs the product photography the project does not have, so renders would be authored line-art.
